units.zh: 孔崇弼，初仕後唐，自吏部郎中授給事中，時族兄昭序繇給事中改左常侍，兄弟同居門下，時論榮之。
units.en: Kong Chongbi began his career under Later Tang. Promoted from director in the Ministry of Personnel to supervising censor, he served at the same time as his older kinsman Zhaoxu, who had moved from supervising censor to left regular attendant. With both brothers holding posts in the Secretariat, contemporaries took it as a mark of family distinction.
units.literal: Kong Chongbi at first served Later Tang; from Director in the Ministry of Personnel he was appointed Supervising Censor. At that time his clansman elder brother Zhaoxu moved from Supervising Censor to Left Regular Attendant. The brothers both dwelt together under the Gate of the Imperial Secretariat, and contemporaries regarded it as an honor.

units.zh: 崇弼，天福中遷左散騎常侍。
units.en: During the Tianfu era Chongbi was promoted to left regular attendant of the cavalry.
units.literal: Chongbi, during Tianfu, was transferred to Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

units.zh: 無他才，但能談笑，戲玩人物，揚眉抵掌，取悅於人。
units.en: He possessed no other ability, yet he could banter and jest, mock people to their faces, arch his brows and clap his hands in amusement, and win others' favor.
units.literal: He had no other talent but could jest and banter, play with people's characters, arch his brows and slap his palms together, and please others.

units.zh: 五年，詔令泛海使於杭越。
units.en: In the fifth year of the reign he was ordered by imperial edict to go by sea as envoy to Hang and Yue.
units.literal: In the fifth year an edict ordered him as envoy by sea to Hang and Yue.

units.zh: 先是，浙中贈賄，每歲恒及萬緡，時議者曰：「孔常侍命奇薄，何消盈數，有命即無財，有財即無命。」
units.en: Before this, tribute gifts from Zhejiang routinely amounted to ten thousand strings of cash a year. People at court remarked, "Vice Censor Kong's fate is unusually meager—why should he need a fortune? Appointment and profit never come together for him: if he gets the post he will have no money, and if he has money he will not live to enjoy it."
units.literal: Previously, gifts from Zhe reached ten thousand strings of cash every year. Commentators of the time said: "Vice Censor Kong's fate is strangely thin—why need such a full sum? When there is an appointment there is no wealth; when there is wealth there is no life."

units.zh: 明年使還，果海中船壞，空手而歸。
units.en: The following year, when the mission returned, the ships were indeed lost at sea, and he came home with nothing.
units.literal: The next year when the envoy returned, indeed the ships were wrecked at sea, and he came back empty-handed.

units.zh: 〈（案：以下殘闕。）〉

units.zh: 陳保極，閩中人也。
units.en: Chen Baoji was a native of Fujian.
units.literal: Chen Baoji was a man of Minzhong.

units.zh: 好學，善屬文，後唐天成中擢進士第，秦王從榮聞其名，辟為從事。
units.en: Fond of study and skilled in prose, he passed the jinshi examination in the Tiancheng era of Later Tang. When Prince of Qin Congrong heard of him, he took him on as a staff officer.
units.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at literary composition. In the Tiancheng era of Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination. Prince of Qin Congrong heard his name and recruited him as an aide.

units.zh: 從榮素急暴，後怒保極不告出遊宰相門，以馬箠鞭之，尋出為定州推官。
units.en: Congrong was naturally violent and impulsive. He later flew into a rage because Baoji had visited the chief ministers without telling him, and lashed him with a riding crop. Baoji was soon transferred out to serve as investigating officer in Dingzhou.
units.literal: Congrong was by nature violent and quick-tempered. Later he grew angry that Baoji had gone out to visit the chief ministers' gates without informing him, and beat him with a horse whip; soon afterward he was sent out as investigating officer of Ding prefecture.

units.zh: 從榮敗，執政知其屈，擢居三署，歷禮部、倉部員外郎。
units.en: After Congrong's downfall the court recognized that Baoji had been treated unjustly and promoted him into the Three Bureaus, where he served successively as vice director in the ministries of rites and of granaries.
units.literal: When Congrong was defeated, those in power knew he had been wronged and promoted him to the Three Bureaus, serving in succession as vice director in the Ministries of Rites and of Granaries.

units.zh: 初，桑維翰登第之歲，保極時在秦王幕下，因戲謂同輩曰：「近知今歲有三個半人及第。」
units.en: When Sang Weihan took his degree, Baoji was still on the prince of Qin's staff. He joked to his colleagues, "I've just heard that three and a half men passed the examination this year."
units.literal: Earlier, in the year Sang Weihan passed the examination, Baoji was then on the Prince of Qin's staff. In jest he told his colleagues: "I have just learned that this year three and a half men passed."

units.zh: 蓋其年收四人，保極以維翰短陋，故謂之半人也。
units.en: Four candidates had in fact passed that year, but because Weihan was short and plain-looking, Baoji counted him as only half a man.
units.literal: For that year four were admitted; Baoji, because Weihan was short and homely, therefore called him half a man.

units.zh: 天福中，維翰既居相位，保極時在曹郎，慮除官差跌，心不自安，乃乞假南遊，將謀退跡。
units.en: In the Tianfu era, once Weihan had become chief minister, Baoji was serving as a bureau secretary. Fearful of being demoted, he grew uneasy and asked leave to travel south, planning to retire from office.
units.literal: During Tianfu, after Weihan had taken the chief ministership, Baoji was then a bureau secretary. Fearing a demotion in office, he was ill at ease in mind and asked leave to travel south, intending to withdraw from public life.

units.zh: 既而襄、鄧長吏以行止入奏，維翰乃奏於高祖曰：「保極閩人，多狡，恐逃入淮海。」
units.en: Soon the senior officials of Xiang and Deng reported his movements to court. Weihan then told Gaozu, "Baoji is a Fujian man and notoriously cunning; I fear he may flee to the Huaihai region."
units.literal: Soon the chief officials of Xiang and Deng reported his movements to the throne. Weihan then memorialized Gaozu: "Baoji is a man of Min, very crafty; I fear he may flee into the Huaihai region."

units.zh: 即以詔追赴闕，將下臺鍛成其事，同列李崧極言以解之，因令所司就所居鞫之，貶為衛尉寺丞，仍奪金紫。
units.en: An edict immediately recalled him to the capital. The authorities were about to hand him over to the censorate and manufacture a criminal case, but his colleague Li Song argued forcefully on his behalf. The court then ordered an inquiry at his home. He was demoted to assistant director in the Court of Imperial Regalia and stripped of his gold seal and purple robe.
units.literal: An edict at once recalled him to court. They were about to send him to the censorate and forge the case into a crime, but his colleague Li Song spoke strongly to clear him. Thereupon the authorities were ordered to try him at his residence. He was demoted to assistant director of the Court of Imperial Regalia and stripped of his gold seal and purple robe.

units.zh: 尋復為倉部員外郎，竟以銜憤而卒。
units.en: He was soon restored as vice director in the ministry of granaries, but in the end died still brooding over the injustice.
units.literal: Soon he was restored as vice director in the Ministry of Granaries, but in the end died nursing resentment.

units.zh: 保極無時才，有傲人之名，而性復鄙吝，所得利祿，未嘗奉身，但蔬食而已。
units.en: Baoji had no real talent for public life and was known for looking down on others, yet he was also miserly by nature. He never spent his salary on himself and lived on nothing but plain fare.
units.literal: Baoji had no talent for his times and bore a reputation for arrogance toward others, yet his nature was also mean and stingy. The salary and emoluments he received he never spent on himself but ate only plain vegetables.

units.zh: 每與人奕棋，敗則以手亂其局，蓋拒所賭金錢不欲償也。
units.en: Whenever he played chess and lost, he would sweep the pieces off the board with his hand, plainly to avoid paying what he had wagered.
units.literal: Whenever he played chess with others and lost, he would scramble the board with his hand—clearly refusing to pay the money staked.

units.zh: 及卒，室無妻兒，帷囊中貯白金十鋌，為他人所有，時甚嗤之。
units.en: When he died he left no wife or children. In a pouch in his room were ten ingots of silver that belonged to someone else, and contemporaries mocked him roundly for it.
units.literal: When he died his household had no wife or children. In a curtain pouch were stored ten ingots of white gold belonging to someone else, and people of the time greatly ridiculed him.

units.zh: 王瑜，其先范陽人也。
units.en: Wang Yu's family came from Fanyang.
units.literal: Wang Yu's ancestors were from Fanyang.

units.zh: 父欽祚，仕至殿中監，出為義州刺史。
units.en: His father Qinhuo rose to director of the palace domestic service and was later posted as prefect of Yi.
units.literal: His father Qinhuo rose in office to Director of the Palace Domestic Service and went out as prefect of Yi.

units.zh: 瑜性兇狡，然雋辯驍果，騎射刀筆之長，亦稱於當代。
units.en: Yu was by nature violent and treacherous, yet he was quick-witted, eloquent, and bold in battle, and his skill at riding, archery, and administrative writing also won him a name in his day.
units.literal: Yu by nature was fierce and cunning, yet he was eloquent, brave, and resolute; his skill in horsemanship, archery, and the brush also won praise in his generation.

units.zh: 起家累為從事。
units.en: He began his career as a series of staff appointments.
units.literal: From his first appointment he repeatedly served as an aide.

units.zh: 天福中，授左贊善大夫。
units.en: In the Tianfu era he was appointed left mentor.
units.literal: During Tianfu he was appointed Left Mentor.

units.zh: 會濮郡秋稼豐衍，稅籍不均，命乘使車，按察定計。
units.en: When Pu prefecture had a bumper autumn harvest but uneven tax rolls, he was sent out in the envoy carriage to inspect the district and set the levies right.
units.literal: It happened that in Pu prefecture the autumn harvest was abundant but the tax registers were uneven, so he was ordered to ride the envoy carriage and inspect and fix the assessments.

units.zh: 既至郡，謂校簿吏胡蘊、惠鶚曰：「余食貧久矣，室無增資，為我致意縣宰，且求假貸。」
units.en: On reaching the prefecture he told the registry clerks Hu Yun and Hui E, "I have been poor for years and my household has no spare funds. Pass word to the county magistrates for me and ask them for a loan."
units.literal: When he reached the prefecture he said to the registry clerks Hu Yun and Hui E: "I have been poor in food for a long time and my household has no added wealth. Convey my regards to the county magistrates and ask them for loans."

units.zh: 由是濮之部內五邑令長共斂錢五十萬，私獻於瑜。
units.en: The magistrates of the five counties in Pu then pooled five hundred thousand cash and secretly gave it to Yu.
units.literal: Thereupon the magistrates of the five districts within Pu together collected five hundred thousand cash and privately presented it to Yu.

units.zh: 瑜即以書上奏，高祖覽章嘆曰：「廉直清慎有如此者，誠良臣也。」
units.en: Yu then submitted a memorial. When Gaozu read it he exclaimed, "Such integrity, uprightness, purity, and caution—this is truly a fine minister."
units.literal: Yu thereupon memorialized in writing. Gaozu read the memorial and sighed: "Integrity, uprightness, purity, and caution such as this—truly a fine minister."

units.zh: 於是二吏五宰即時停黜，擢瑜為太府少卿。
units.en: The two clerks and five magistrates were immediately dismissed, and Yu was promoted to vice director of the imperial storehouse.
units.literal: Thereupon the two clerks and five magistrates were at once dismissed, and Yu was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse.

units.zh: 杜重威之鎮東平也，瑜父欽祚為節度副使，及重威移鎮常山，瑜乃詭計於重威，使奏己為恒州節度副使，竟代其父位。
units.en: While Du Chongwei held Dongping, Yu's father Qinhuo served as his deputy. When Chongwei was transferred to Changshan, Yu persuaded him by a ruse to recommend him as deputy military governor of Hengzhou, and in the end took his father's place.
units.literal: When Du Chongwei governed Dongping, Yu's father Qinhuo was military governor's deputy. When Chongwei was transferred to govern Changshan, Yu devised a stratagem with Chongwei and had him memorialize that Yu himself should be deputy military governor of Heng, and in the end replaced his father's post.

units.zh: 歲餘，入為刑部郎中。
units.en: After a little more than a year he was recalled to the capital as director in the ministry of punishments.
units.literal: After more than a year he entered the capital as Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

units.zh: 丙午歲，父欽祚刺舉義州，瑜歸寧至郡。
units.en: In the bingwu year his father Qinhuo was posted as investigating commissioner of Yi prefecture, and Yu went to visit him there.
units.literal: In the bingwu year his father Qinhuo was investigating commissioner of Yi prefecture, and Yu went home on a visit to the prefecture.

units.zh: 會契丹據有中夏，何建以秦州歸蜀，瑜說欽祚曰：「若不西走，當屬契丹矣！」
units.en: The Khitans had seized the heartland, and He Jian had surrendered Qinzhou to Shu. Yu urged his father, "If we do not flee west, we shall end up under Khitan rule!"
units.literal: It happened that the Khitans held the Central Plains and He Jian surrendered Qin prefecture to Shu. Yu urged Qinhuo: "If we do not flee west, we shall fall under the Khitans!"

units.zh: 厲色數諫，其父怒而不從。
units.en: He remonstrated again and again with a fierce expression, but his father grew angry and refused.
units.literal: With stern countenance he remonstrated repeatedly; his father grew angry and would not follow.

units.zh: 因其臥疾涉旬，瑜仗劍而脅之曰：「老懦無謀，欲趨炮烙。
units.en: When his father had been bedridden for more than ten days, Yu drew his sword and threatened him: "You old fool without a plan—you are rushing straight toward the stake.
units.literal: Because he had lain ill for more than ten days, Yu took sword in hand and threatened him: "Old coward without a plan—you wish to rush toward the burning stake.

units.zh: 不即為計，則死於刃下。」
units.en: If you do not act now, you die by this blade."
units.literal: If you do not decide at once, you die beneath the blade."

units.zh: 父不得已而聽之。
units.en: His father had no choice but to yield.
units.literal: His father had no choice but to obey.

units.zh: 時隴東屯兵扼其川路，將北趣蕃部假途，而因與郡盜酋長趙徽歃血為約，以兄事之。
units.en: Garrison troops in eastern Long blocked the river routes, so they planned to head north through tribal territory and borrow a passage. Yu then swore a blood oath with Zhao Hui, a local bandit chieftain, and treated him as an elder brother.
units.literal: At that time Longdong garrison troops blocked the river routes. They intended to go north toward the tribal lands to borrow a passage, and therefore with Zhao Hui, chieftain of the local bandits in the prefecture, they made a blood oath and treated him as an elder brother.

units.zh: 謂徽曰：「西至成都，余身為相，余父為將，爾當領一大郡，能遂行乎？」
units.en: He told Hui, "When we reach Chengdu, I shall become chief minister and my father a general, and you shall govern a great prefecture. Will you go through with this?"
units.literal: He said to Hui: "When we reach Chengdu in the west, I shall become chief minister and my father a general; you shall hold a great prefecture. Can you go through with the journey?"

units.zh: 徽曰：「諾。」
units.en: Hui answered, "Agreed."
units.literal: Hui said: "Agreed."

units.zh: 瑜慮為所賣，先致其妻孥，館於郡中。
units.en: Fearing betrayal, Yu first sent Hui's wife and children to stay in the prefectural seat as hostages.
units.literal: Yu feared being betrayed and first sent Hui's wife and children to lodge in the prefectural city.

units.zh: 行有期矣，徽潛召其黨，伺於郊外。
units.en: When the day of departure was fixed, Hui secretly gathered his men and waited in ambush outside the city.
units.literal: When the day of departure was set, Hui secretly summoned his followers and lay in wait in the suburbs.

units.zh: 子夜，瑜舉族行，輜重絡繹十有餘里。
units.en: At midnight Yu set out with his entire clan, their baggage train stretching more than ten li along the road.
units.literal: At midnight Yu moved with his whole clan; baggage trains stretched in an unbroken line for more than ten li.

units.zh: 徽之所親，循溝澮而遁，至馬峽路隅，舉燧相應，其黨起於伏莽，斷欽祚之首，貫諸長矛。
units.en: Hui's men stole along ditches and canals until, at a bend on the Maxia road, they lit signal fires. His band sprang from the brush, cut off Qinhuo's head, and spitted it on a long spear.
units.literal: Hui's intimates stole along ditches and canals. At a corner of the road at Maxia they raised beacon fires in answer to one another; his band rose from ambush in the thickets, cut off Qinhuo's head, and threaded it on a long spear.

units.zh: 平生聚蓄金幣萬計，皆為賊所掠，少長百口，殺之殆盡。
units.en: The gold and cash he had amassed over a lifetime—tens of thousands in all—were looted by the bandits, and of more than a hundred kin young and old, nearly all were slaughtered.
units.literal: Gold and coin he had amassed in his lifetime, numbering in the tens of thousands, were all plundered by the bandits; of more than a hundred persons young and old, nearly all were killed.

units.zh: 瑜尚獨戰千人，矢不虛發，手無射捍，其指流血。
units.en: Yu still fought on alone against a thousand men; every arrow he loosed found its mark. He had no archer's thumb guard, and his fingers ran with blood.
units.literal: Yu still fought alone against a thousand; not an arrow missed its mark. He had no thumb guard for shooting, and his fingers bled.

units.zh: 及窘，乃夜竄山谷，落發為僧。
units.en: When he was cornered, he fled by night into the hills, shaved his head, and took the tonsure.
units.literal: When hard pressed, he fled by night into the mountains and valleys, shaved his head, and became a monk.

units.zh: 月餘，為樵人所獲，縶送岐州，為侯益所殺，時年三十九。
units.en: After more than a month woodcutters captured him and sent him bound to Qizhou, where Hou Yi had him executed. He was thirty-nine.
units.literal: After more than a month he was seized by woodcutters, bound, and sent to Qi prefecture, where Hou Yi had him killed. He was thirty-nine.

units.zh: 始瑜有姑寡居，來歸其家，以前夫遺腹有子，經數年不產，每因事預告人吉兇，無不驗者。
units.en: Yu had an aunt, a widow, who came to live in his household. She was said to be carrying her late husband's posthumous child, yet for years she bore none; still, whenever she foretold good or ill fortune, her predictions always came true.
units.literal: Earlier Yu had an aunt who lived as a widow and came to join his household. Because her former husband's posthumous child was said to be in her womb, for several years she did not give birth, yet whenever she foretold fortune or misfortune on some matter, it never failed to come true.

units.zh: 時契丹入中闕，前月餘謂瑜曰：「暴兵將至，宜速去之，茍不去，亂必及矣。」
units.en: When the Khitans entered the capital, more than a month beforehand she told Yu, "Violent soldiers are coming—you must leave at once. If you stay, calamity will overtake you."
units.literal: When the Khitans entered the central capital, more than a month before she told Yu: "Violent troops are coming; you should flee quickly. If you do not go, disorder will surely reach you."

units.zh: 後瑜果死，此謂「天作孽，猶可違；
units.en: Yu did indeed die afterward. This was a case of the saying, "When Heaven sends disaster, one may still escape it;
units.literal: Later Yu indeed died. This illustrates the saying: "When Heaven sends calamity, it may still be avoided;

units.zh: 自作孽，不可逭」也。
units.en: but when a man brings disaster on himself, there is no escaping it."
units.literal: when one brings calamity on oneself, it cannot be escaped."

units.zh: 張繼祚，故齊王全義之子也。
units.en: Zhang Jizuo was a son of the former prince of Qi, Quanyi.
units.literal: Zhang Jizuo was a son of the former Prince of Qi, Quanyi.

units.zh: 始為河南府衙內指揮使，全義卒，除金吾將軍，旋授蔡州刺史，累官至檢校太保。
units.en: He began as commander of the Henan prefectural guard. After Quanyi's death he was made a general of the golden crow guard, soon received appointment as prefect of Cai, and eventually rose to honorary grand guardian.
units.literal: At first he was commander of the Henan prefectural guard; when Quanyi died he was made general of the Golden Crow guard, soon appointed prefect of Cai, and rose in office to honorary Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 明宗郊天，充供頓使，復除西衛上將軍。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong sacrificed to Heaven at the suburbs, Jizuo served as provisioning commissioner and was again appointed general of the western guard.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven, he served as provisioning commissioner and was again appointed general of the Western Guard.

units.zh: 唐清泰末，丁母憂。
units.en: At the end of Tang's Qingtai era he went into mourning for his mother.
units.literal: At the end of the Qingtai era of Tang he entered mourning for his mother.

units.zh: 天福初，喪制未闋，會張從賓作亂，發兵迫脅，取赴河陽，令知留守事。
units.en: Early in the Tianfu era, before his mourning period had ended, Zhang Congbin rebelled, raised troops, and forced him along. He was taken to Heyang and put in charge of the regency.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, before his mourning term had ended, Zhang Congbin rebelled, raised troops, and coerced him; he was taken to Heyang and ordered to manage the regency affairs.

units.zh: 從賓敗，與二子詔戮於市。
units.en: When Congbin was defeated, he and his two sons were executed by imperial order in the marketplace.
units.literal: When Congbin was defeated, he and his two sons were executed by imperial edict in the marketplace.

units.zh: 始繼祚與範延光有舊，嘗遣人以馬遺之。
units.en: Jizuo had earlier been on friendly terms with Fan Yanguang and once sent him horses as a gift.
units.literal: Earlier Jizuo had been on friendly terms with Fan Yanguang and once sent someone to present him with horses.

units.zh: 屬朝廷起兵，將討鄴城，為巡兵所獲，奏之，高祖深忌之。
units.en: When the court marched to attack Ye, patrol troops seized the gift and reported it, and Gaozu took deep offense.
units.literal: When the court raised troops to attack Ye, the gift was seized by patrol soldiers and reported; Gaozu deeply resented it.

units.zh: 及敗，宰臣桑維翰以父珙早事齊王，奏欲雪之，高祖不允，
units.en: After the defeat, chief minister Sang Weihan—whose father Gong had long served the prince of Qi—memorialized to clear the family's name, but Gaozu refused,
units.literal: When he was defeated, the chief minister Sang Weihan, because his father Gong had long served the Prince of Qi, memorialized to clear the family, but Gaozu would not agree,

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：史館修撰李濤上言：張全義有再造洛邑之功，乞免其族。
units.en: (Comprehensive Mirror: Li Tao of the historiography institute memorialized that Zhang Quanyi had restored Luoyang and asked that his clan be spared.
units.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: Li Tao, reviser of the Historiography Institute, memorialized: Zhang Quanyi had the merit of restoring Luoyang; I beg that his clan be spared.

units.zh: 遂止誅繼祚妻子。）〉
units.en: The execution of Jizuo's wife and children was then halted.)〉
units.literal: Thereupon the execution of Jizuo's wife and children was halted.)〉

units.zh: 遂止罪繼祚一房，不累其族。
units.en: Punishment was thus limited to Jizuo's own household and did not extend to his wider clan.
units.literal: Thus punishment stopped at Jizuo's own household and did not extend to his clan.

units.zh: 鄭阮，洺州人也。
units.en: Zheng Ruan was a native of Mingzhou.
units.literal: Zheng Ruan was a man of Mingzhou.

units.zh: 少為本部牙將，唐莊宗略地山東，以阮首歸義旗，繼遷軍職。
units.en: In youth he served as a military adjutant of his circuit. When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang conquered eastern Shandong, Ruan was the first to rally to the loyalist cause and thereafter rose through military ranks.
units.literal: In youth he served as a military adjutant of his circuit. When Tang Zhuangzong swept through eastern Shandong, Ruan was the first to join the loyalist banner, and thereafter rose through military posts.

units.zh: 阮有子，自幼事明宗中門使安重誨，重誨以其桀黠，愛之。
units.en: Ruan had a son who from childhood served An Chonghui, Mingzong's middle-gate commissioner. Chonghui took a liking to him for his clever boldness.
units.literal: Ruan had a son who from childhood served An Chonghui, the middle-gate commissioner under Emperor Mingzong. Chonghui loved him for his shrewd boldness.

units.zh: 及明宗即位，擢阮至鳳翔節度副使。
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne, Ruan was promoted to deputy military governor of Fengxiang.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Ruan was promoted to deputy military governor of Fengxiang.

units.zh: 會末帝鎮其地，阮稍狎之。
units.en: When the Last Emperor governed the region, Ruan grew somewhat familiar with him.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor governed that region, Ruan grew somewhat familiar with him.

units.zh: 末帝嗣位，以阮為趙州刺史。
units.en: When the Last Emperor succeeded to the throne, he appointed Ruan prefect of Zhao.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded to the throne, he appointed Ruan prefect of Zhao.

units.zh: 而阮性貪濁，民間細務，皆密察而紀之，令納賂以贖罪。
units.en: But Ruan was greedy and corrupt. He secretly investigated and recorded every petty matter among the people and demanded bribes to redeem offenses.
units.literal: But Ruan was greedy and corrupt. He secretly investigated and recorded every petty matter among the people and ordered bribes to redeem offenses.

units.zh: 有屬邑令，因科醵拒命，密以束素募人陰求其過，後竟停其職，人甚非之。
units.en: When a subordinate county magistrate refused a levy assessment, Ruan secretly hired men with cloth bribes to find his faults; the magistrate was eventually removed from office, to widespread condemnation.
units.literal: A subordinate county magistrate, refusing a levy assessment, was secretly pursued by men hired with cloth bribes to find his faults; he was eventually removed from office, to public condemnation.

units.zh: 又嘗以郡符取部內兇肆中人隸其籍者，遣於青州，舁喪至洺，郡人憚其遠，願輸直百緡以免其行，阮本無喪，即受直放還。
units.en: He also once used a prefectural order to take a registered man from an undertaker's shop in his territory and send him to Qingzhou to carry a coffin back to Ming. Dreading the distance, the people offered one hundred strings of cash to be spared the journey. Ruan had no bereavement of his own, yet accepted the payment and released the man.
units.literal: He also once used a prefectural order to take a registered man from the undertaker's shop within his territory and send him to Qingzhou to bear a coffin back to Ming; the people, dreading the distance, offered one hundred strings of cash to be spared the journey. Ruan had no actual bereavement, yet accepted the payment and released the man.

units.zh: 識者曰：「此非吉兆也。」
units.en: The knowing said, "This is no good omen."
units.literal: The knowing said, "This is no good omen."

units.zh: 未幾，改曹州刺史，為政愈弊。
units.en: Before long he was transferred to be prefect of Cao, and his governance grew still more corrupt.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred to be prefect of Cao, and his governance grew still more corrupt.

units.zh: 高祖建義入洛，阮自郡來朝，旋為本州指揮使石重立所殺，舉族無孑遺。
units.en: When Gaozu raised the righteous cause and entered Luoyang, Ruan came from his prefecture to court and was soon killed by Shi Chongli, commander of his native prefecture, with his entire clan wiped out to the last.
units.literal: When Gaozu raised the righteous cause and entered Luoyang, Ruan came from his prefecture to court and was soon killed by Shi Chongli, commander of his native prefecture, with his entire clan wiped out to the last.

units.zh: 胡饒，大梁人也。
units.en: Hu Rao was a native of Daliang.
units.literal: Hu Rao was a man of Daliang.

units.zh: 少事本鎮連帥為都吏，歷馬步都虞候。
units.en: In youth he served the circuit military governor as chief clerk and later held the post of combined cavalry and infantry commandant.
units.literal: In youth he served the military governor of his circuit as chief clerk and rose through the posts of cavalry and infantry commandant.

units.zh: 會唐明宗鎮其地，與部將王建立相善，明宗即位，建立領常山，奏饒為真定少尹。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong of Tang governed the region, Rao was on good terms with the staff general Wang Jianli. After Mingzong took the throne, Jianli governed Changshan and recommended Rao as vice prefect of Zhending.
units.literal: When Tang Emperor Mingzong governed that region he was on good terms with the staff general Wang Jianli. When Mingzong took the throne, Jianli governed Changshan and recommended Rao as vice prefect of Zhending.

units.zh: 饒本憸人，既在府幕，無士君子之風。
units.en: Rao was crafty by nature, and once he joined the governor's staff he showed none of a gentleman's conduct.
units.literal: Rao was by nature a crafty man; once in the governor's staff he had none of a gentleman's bearing.

units.zh: 嘗因事趙郡，有平棘令張鵬者獻策，請建立於境內每縣所管鄉置鄉直一人，令月書縣令出入行止，饒乃導而薦焉。
units.en: On a mission to Zhao commandery he met Zhang Peng, magistrate of Pingji, who proposed that Jianli appoint one village overseer in every township under each county, with monthly reports on each magistrate's movements. Rao promoted the scheme.
units.literal: Once on business in Zhao commandery he met Zhang Peng, magistrate of Pingji, who offered a plan asking Jianli to place one village overseer in every township under each county in his territory, with orders that each month they record the magistrate's comings and goings. Rao guided and recommended the plan.

units.zh: 建立行之彌年，詞訟蜂起，四郡大擾。
units.en: Jianli enforced the plan for a full year, lawsuits multiplied, and all four commanderies were thrown into turmoil.
units.literal: Jianli carried it out for a full year; lawsuits swarmed like bees and the four commanderies were greatly disturbed.

units.zh: 天成末，王都構亂，陰使結建立為兄弟之國。
units.en: Late in the Tiancheng era Wang Du plotted rebellion and secretly sent envoys to win Jianli into a pact of allied states.
units.literal: At the end of Tiancheng, Wang Du plotted rebellion and secretly sent envoys to bind Jianli in a pact of brother states.

units.zh: 時饒又曾薦梁時右庶子張澄為判官，建立亦狎之。
units.en: Rao had also recommended Zhang Cheng, former right assistant to the heir apparent under Liang, as administrative aide, and Jianli was on familiar terms with him.
units.literal: At that time Rao had also recommended Zhang Cheng, former right assistant to the heir apparent under Liang, as administrative aide, and Jianli was intimate with him as well.

units.zh: 澄素不知書，每座則以《陰府》、《鬼谷》為己任。
units.en: Cheng was barely literate and at every gathering treated the Yin Fu and Guiguzi as his specialties.
units.literal: Cheng by nature did not know books; whenever he took his seat he made the Yin Fu and Guiguzi his stock in trade.

units.zh: 建立時密以王都之盟告之，澄與饒俱贊成其事，會王師圍中山，其事遂寢，而饒之兇戾如此。
units.en: Jianli secretly disclosed Wang Du's alliance to them, and both Cheng and Rao urged it on. When imperial troops besieged Zhongshan the plot came to nothing, but Rao's brutality and perversity were of this sort.
units.literal: Jianli at the time secretly told them of Wang Du's alliance; Cheng and Rao both approved the affair. When imperial troops besieged Zhongshan the matter then collapsed, yet Rao's violence and perversity were such as this.

units.zh: 清泰初，馮道出鎮同州，饒時為副使，道以重臣，稀於接洽，饒忿之，每乘酒於牙門詬道，道必延入，待以酒肴，致敬而退。
units.en: Early in the Qingtai era Feng Dao was posted to govern Tongzhou with Rao as his deputy. As a senior minister Feng Dao rarely received callers, and Rao resented it. Drunk, he would abuse Feng Dao at headquarters, but Feng Dao always invited him in, served wine and food, paid his respects, and let him go.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, Feng Dao went out to govern Tong prefecture and Rao was then his deputy. Because Dao was a great minister he seldom received visitors; Rao resented this and, whenever drunk, would revile Dao at the headquarters gate. Dao always invited him in, entertained him with wine and food, paid his respects, and sent him away.

units.zh: 道謂左右曰：「此人為不善，自當有報，吾何怒焉。」
units.en: Feng Dao told his attendants, "This man does wrong; retribution will come to him in its own time—why should I grow angry?"
units.literal: Dao told those beside him: "This man does evil; he will have his own retribution—why should I be angry?"

units.zh: 饒後閑居河陽。
units.en: Rao later lived in retirement at Heyang.
units.literal: Later Rao lived in retirement at Heyang.

units.zh: 天福二年夏，會張從賓作亂，饒謁於麾下，請預其行。
units.en: In the summer of the second Tianfu year, when Zhang Congbin rebelled, Rao came to his camp and asked to march with him.
units.literal: In the summer of the second year of Tianfu, when Zhang Congbin rebelled, Rao presented himself at his headquarters and asked to join the campaign.

units.zh: 從賓敗，饒以王建立方鎮平盧，走投之，建立延入城，斬之以聞，聞者快焉。
units.en: When Congbin was defeated, Rao fled to Wang Jianli, who was then military governor of Pinglu. Jianli had him brought into the city, beheaded him, and reported it to court; all who heard of it were glad.
units.literal: When Congbin was defeated, Rao, because Wang Jianli was then military governor of Pinglu, fled to seek him. Jianli had him brought into the city and beheaded him, then reported it; those who heard rejoiced.

units.zh: 劉遂清，字得一，青州北海人，梁開封尹鄩之猶子也。
units.en: Liu Suiqing, styled Deyi, was from Beihai in Qingzhou and was a nephew by marriage of Zheng, Liang's chief minister of Kaifeng.
units.literal: Liu Suiqing, style Deyi, was a man of Beihai in Qing prefecture, a nephew by marriage of Zheng, chief minister of Kaifeng under Liang.

units.zh: 父琪，以鴻臚卿致仕。
units.en: His father Qi had retired as minister of the court of imperial entertainments.
units.literal: His father Qi retired as Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

units.zh: 遂清少敏惠，初仕梁為保鑾軍使，歷內諸司使，莊宗入汴，不改其職。
units.en: Suiqing was clever from youth. He first served Liang as commissioner of the palace guard, then held a series of posts as commissioner of the inner bureaus; when Zhuangzong entered Bian his offices were left unchanged.
units.literal: Suiqing in youth was quick and clever. He first served Liang as commissioner of the Palace Guard and passed through the posts of commissioner of the inner bureaus; when Zhuangzong entered Bian he did not change his office.

units.zh: 明宗即位，加檢校尚書僕射，委以西都監守。
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne he was given the honorary title of vice director of the masters of writing and charged with guarding the western capital.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was given the honorary title of Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and entrusted with guarding the western capital.

units.zh: 逾歲，以中山王都有不臣之跡，除遂清為易州刺史，俾遏其寇沖，既至郡，大有禦侮之略，境內賴焉。
units.en: A year later, when Wang Du of Zhongshan showed signs of rebellion, Suiqing was appointed prefect of Yi to block his raids. On reaching the prefecture he devised strong defenses, and the region came to rely on him.
units.literal: After a year, because Wang Du of Zhongshan showed signs of disloyalty, Suiqing was appointed prefect of Yi to block his raiding thrusts. Once he reached the prefecture he had great plans for defense, and the territory relied on him.

units.zh: 王都平，加檢校司空，遷棣州刺史。
units.en: After Wang Du was pacified he was given the honorary title of minister of works and transferred to prefect of Di.
units.literal: When Wang Du was pacified he was given the honorary title of Minister of Works and transferred to prefect of Di.

units.zh: 天成、長興中，歷典淄、興、登三郡，咸有善政。
units.en: During the Tiancheng and Changxing eras he governed in turn Zi, Xing, and Deng, and in each place earned a reputation for good government.
units.literal: During Tiancheng and Changxing he governed in succession the three prefectures of Zi, Xing, and Deng, and in each had good administration.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒潞王紀》：帝之起鳳翔也，召興州刺史劉遂清，遲疑不至。
units.en: (Comprehensive Mirror, Annals of the Prince of Lu: When the emperor rose at Fengxiang he summoned Liu Suiqing, prefect of Xing, but Suiqing hesitated and did not come.
units.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror, Annals of Prince of Lu: When the emperor rose at Fengxiang he summoned Liu Suiqing, prefect of Xing, but he hesitated and did not come.

units.zh: 聞帝入洛，乃悉集三泉、西縣、金牛、桑林戍兵以歸，自散關以南，城鎮悉棄之，皆為蜀人所有。
units.en: On hearing that the emperor had entered Luoyang, he gathered the garrisons of Sanquan, Xixian, Jinniu, and Sanglin and withdrew. From Sanguan Pass southward he abandoned every town and fort, and all fell to Shu.
units.literal: When he heard that the emperor had entered Luoyang, he then gathered all the garrison troops of Sanquan, Xixian, Jinniu, and Sanglin and withdrew. From Sanguan Pass southward, every town and fort was abandoned and all fell into Shu hands.

units.zh: 入朝，帝欲治罪，以其能自歸，乃赦之。）〉
units.en: When he presented himself at court the emperor wished to punish him, but because he had come back of his own accord he was pardoned.)〉
units.literal: When he came to court the emperor wished to punish him, but because he had returned of his own accord he was pardoned.)〉

units.zh: 高祖即位之二年，授鳳州防禦使，加檢校司徒，會丁母憂，起復，授內客省使、右監門衛大將軍。
units.en: In the second year of Gaozu's reign he was made defense commissioner of Fengzhou and given the honorary title of minister of education. When his mother died he was recalled from mourning and appointed commissioner of the inner guests bureau and great general of the right gate guard.
units.literal: In the second year after Gaozu's accession he was made defense commissioner of Feng prefecture and given the honorary title of Minister of Education. When he entered mourning for his mother he was recalled from mourning and appointed commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau and great general of the Right Gate Guard.

units.zh: 六年，駕幸鄴都，轉宣徽北院使兼判三司，加檢校太保。
units.en: In the sixth year, when the emperor visited Yedu, he was made commissioner of the northern bureau of the palace secretariat with concurrent charge of the three bureaus and given the honorary title of grand guardian.
units.literal: In the sixth year, when the imperial carriage visited Yedu, he was transferred to commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat with concurrent charge of the Three Bureaus and given the honorary title of Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 七年，少帝嗣位，加右領軍衛上將軍，仍賜竭誠翊戴保節功臣。
units.en: In the seventh year, when the young emperor succeeded, he was made general of the right army guard and granted the title of meritorious minister for devoted loyalty in supporting the throne and preserving integrity.
units.literal: In the seventh year, when the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made general of the Right Army Guard and was also granted the title of meritorious minister of devoted loyalty in supporting the throne and preserving integrity.

units.zh: 八年，出領鄭州，加檢校太傅。
units.en: In the eighth year he was posted to govern Zhengzhou and given the honorary title of grand tutor.
units.literal: In the eighth year he went out to govern Zheng prefecture and was given the honorary title of Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 開運二年，遷安州防禦使。
units.en: In the second Kaiyun year he was transferred to defense commissioner of Anzhou.
units.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun he was transferred to defense commissioner of An prefecture.

units.zh: 未幾，上表稱疾，詔許就便，回至上蔡，終於郵舍，時三年四月也。
units.en: Before long he memorialized that he was ill; the court allowed him to retire where he pleased. On his way back to Shangcai he died at a courier station in the fourth month of the third year.
units.literal: Before long he memorialized claiming illness; an edict permitted him to retire as convenient. Returning to Shangcai, he died at a post station in the fourth month of the third year.

units.zh: 遂清性至孝，牧淄川日，自北海迎其母赴郡，母既及境，遂清奔馳路側，控轡行數十里，父老觀者如堵，當時榮之。
units.en: Suiqing was deeply filial by nature. While governing Zichuan he went to Beihai to bring his mother to his post. When she reached the prefectural border he ran out to the road, took the reins of her carriage, and walked beside her for miles. The local elders lined the route, and contemporaries praised him for it.
units.literal: Suiqing by nature was deeply filial. While governing Zichuan he went from Beihai to bring his mother to the prefecture. When she reached the border he ran along the roadside, took the reins, and walked several tens of li; the elders who watched were packed like a wall, and people of the time honored him for it.

units.zh: 遂清素不知書，但多計畫，判三司日，每給百官俸料，與判官議曰：「斯輩非盡有才能，多世祿之家，宜澄其汙而留其清者。」
units.en: Suiqing was barely literate but full of schemes. While in charge of the three bureaus, whenever salaries were issued he would tell his aide, "These men are not all capable—many come from hereditary salary families. We ought to sift out the corrupt and keep the honest."
units.literal: Suiqing by nature did not know books but had many schemes. While judging the Three Bureaus, whenever he issued the officials' salaries he would discuss with his administrative aide: "These men do not all have ability; many are hereditary salary families. One should clarify the tainted and keep the clean."

units.zh: 或對曰：「昔唐朝渾、郭、顏、段，每一赦出，以一子出身，率為常制，且延賞垂裕，為國美譚，未有因月給而欲沙汰，恐未當也。」
units.en: Someone objected, "Under Tang, the Hun, Guo, Yan, and Duan families—each amnesty let one son enter office, which became standard practice. Rewarding merit so that bounty reached later generations was counted a national virtue. No one has tried to purge officials over monthly salaries; I fear that would be wrong."
units.literal: Someone replied: "In Tang times the Hun, Guo, Yan, and Duan clans—whenever an amnesty was issued one son would enter office; this was the regular rule, and extending rewards to enrich descendants was praised as a national virtue. Never has anyone sought to purge men because of monthly pay; I fear this would not be fitting."

units.zh: 群論由此減之。
units.en: The proposal was dropped after this exchange.
units.literal: The group's discussion thereby diminished the proposal.

units.zh: 房暠，京兆長安人也。
units.en: Fang Gao was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
units.literal: Fang Gao was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 少為唐宰臣崔魏公家臣，後因亂，客於蒲州。
units.en: In youth he served as a household retainer of the Tang chief minister, the Duke of Wei surnamed Cui; later, amid the turmoil, he sojourned in Puzhou.
units.literal: In youth he served as a household retainer of the Tang chief minister Duke of Wei surnamed Cui; later, amid the turmoil, he sojourned in Puzhou.

units.zh: 天成中，唐末帝出鎮河中，暠於路左迎謁，求事軍門，末帝愛之，使治賓客。
units.en: During Tiancheng, when the Last Emperor of Tang went out to govern Hezhong, Gao met him at the roadside and sought service at headquarters. The Last Emperor took a liking to him and put him in charge of guests.
units.literal: During Tiancheng, when the Last Emperor of Tang went out to govern Hezhong, Gao met him at the roadside and sought service at headquarters. The Last Emperor took a liking to him and had him manage guests.

units.zh: 及末帝登極，歷南北院宣徽使，尋與趙延壽同為樞密使。
units.en: When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, Gao served successively as commissioner of the southern and northern palace secretariat bureaus, and soon shared the post of confidential commissioner with Zhao Yanshou.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, Gao served successively as commissioner of the southern and northern bureaus of the Palace Secretariat, and soon shared the post of confidential commissioner with Zhao Yanshou.

units.zh: 時薛文遇、劉延朗之徒居中用事，暠雖處密地，其聽用之言，十不得三四，但隨勢可否，不為事先。
units.en: At that time Xue Wenyü, Liu Yanlang, and their like held sway at court. Though Gao sat in the innermost councils, only three or four of every ten words he spoke were heeded; he merely assented or demurred as the tide flowed, never taking the lead.
units.literal: At that time Xue Wenyü, Liu Yanlang, and their like held sway at court. Though Gao sat in the innermost councils, only three or four of every ten words he spoke were heeded; he merely assented or demurred as the tide flowed, never taking the lead.

units.zh: 每朝廷有大事，暠與端明學士等環坐會議，多於眾中俯首而睡，其避事也如此。
units.en: Whenever the court faced a great matter, Gao would sit in conference with the academicians of the Hall of Bright Clarity and the like, and often slept with bowed head among the assembly—such was his way of avoiding responsibility.
units.literal: Whenever the court faced a great matter, Gao would sit in conference with the academicians of the Hall of Bright Clarity and the like, and often slept with bowed head among the assembly—such was his way of avoiding responsibility.

units.zh: 高祖即位，以暠濡足閏朝，不專與奪，故特恩原之，命為左驍衛大將軍，留西京。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, since Gao had served under two dynasties and had not monopolized decisions on life and death, he was specially shown grace and pardoned, appointed grand general of the Left Valiant Guards, and kept at the western capital.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, since Gao had wet his feet in two courts and had not monopolized decisions on life and death, he was specially shown grace and pardoned, appointed grand general of the Left Valiant Guards, and kept at the western capital.

units.zh: 開運元年春，卒於洛陽。
units.en: In spring of the first year of Kaiyun he died at Luoyang.
units.literal: In spring of the first year of Kaiyun he died at Luoyang.

units.zh: 孟承誨，大名人也。
units.en: Meng Chenghui was a native of Daming.
units.literal: Meng Chenghui was a man of Daming.

units.zh: 始為本府牙校，遇高祖臨其地，升為客將。
units.en: At first he was a military adjutant of his prefecture; when Gaozu came to the region, he was promoted to guest officer.
units.literal: At first he was a military adjutant of his prefecture; when Gaozu came to the region, he was promoted to guest officer.

units.zh: 後奏為宗城令，秩滿，以百姓舉留，為常山槁城令，皆有善政。
units.en: He was later recommended as magistrate of Zongcheng, and when his term ended the people petitioned to keep him; he was made magistrate of Gaocheng in Changshan, showing good governance in both posts.
units.literal: He was later recommended as magistrate of Zongcheng, and when his term ended the people petitioned to keep him; he was made magistrate of Gaocheng in Changshan, showing good governance in both posts.

units.zh: 高祖有天下，擢為閣門副使，累遷宣徽使，官至檢校司空、太府卿、右武衛大將軍。
units.en: After Gaozu possessed the realm, Chenghui was promoted to deputy gate commissioner, rose through posts to palace secretariat commissioner, and reached the offices of honorary minister of works, grand minister of the court treasury, and grand general of the Right Martial Guards.
units.literal: After Gaozu possessed the realm, Chenghui was promoted to deputy gate commissioner, rose through posts to palace secretariat commissioner, and reached the offices of honorary minister of works, grand minister of the court treasury, and grand general of the Right Martial Guards.

units.zh: 及少帝嗣位，以植性纖巧，善於希旨，復與權臣宦官密相表裏，凡朝廷恩澤美使，必承誨為之，一歲之中，數四不已。
units.en: When the young emperor succeeded, because of his subtle, crafty nature and skill at reading intentions, he again worked in secret concert with powerful officials and eunuchs; every grace mission or favor-bearing embassy from the court went through Chenghui, several times within a single year without cease.
units.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, because of his subtle, crafty nature and skill at reading intentions, he again worked in secret concert with powerful officials and eunuchs; every grace mission or favor-bearing embassy from the court went through Chenghui, several times within a single year without cease.

units.zh: 由是居第華敞，財帛累積。
units.en: Hence his residence grew splendid and broad, and wealth piled up.
units.literal: Hence his residence grew splendid and broad, and wealth piled up.

units.zh: 及契丹入汴，張彥澤引兵逼宮城，少帝召承誨計之，承誨匿身不赴。
units.en: When the Khitans entered Bian, Zhang Yanzhe led troops to press the palace walls. The young emperor summoned Chenghui to counsel him, but Chenghui hid himself and did not come.
units.literal: When the Khitans entered Bian, Zhang Yanzhe led troops to press the palace walls. The Young Emperor summoned Chenghui to counsel him, but Chenghui hid himself and did not come.

units.zh: 少帝既出宮，寓於開封府舍，具以承誨背恩之事告彥澤，令捕而殺之，其妻女並配部族。
units.en: After the young emperor left the palace and lodged at the Kaifeng prefectural offices, he fully told Yanzhe of Chenghui's betrayal of favor and ordered him captured and killed; his wife and daughters were both assigned to tribal peoples.
units.literal: After the Young Emperor left the palace and lodged at the Kaifeng prefectural offices, he fully told Yanzhe of Chenghui's betrayal of favor and ordered him captured and killed; his wife and daughters were both assigned to tribal peoples.

units.zh: 漢高祖即位，詔贈太保。
units.en: When Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Guardian.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 劉繼勛，衛州人也。
units.en: Liu Jixun was a native of Weizhou.
units.literal: Liu Jixun was a man of Weizhou.

units.zh: 唐天成中，高祖鎮鄴都，繼勛時為客將，高祖愛其端謹，籍其名於帳下，從歷數鎮。
units.en: During Tang's Tiancheng era, when Gaozu governed Yedu, Jixun served as a guest officer. Gaozu admired his steady, careful manner, kept him on his staff register, and took him through several provincial postings.
units.literal: During Tiancheng of Tang, when Gaozu governed Yedu, Jixun was then a guest officer. Gaozu loved his upright caution and registered his name in his staff, following him through several postings.

units.zh: 及即位，擢為閣門使，出為淄州刺史，遷澶州防禦使，俄改鄭州，自宣徽北院使拜華州刺史。
units.en: After Gaozu took the throne, Jixun was made gate commissioner, then prefect of Zi, defense commissioner of Chan, and soon of Zheng; from commissioner of the northern palace secretariat bureau he was appointed prefect of Hua.
units.literal: When he took the throne Jixun was promoted to gate commissioner, sent out as prefect of Zi, transferred to defense commissioner of Chan, soon changed to Zheng, and from commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat was appointed prefect of Hua.

units.zh: 歲餘，鎮同州。
units.en: After a little more than a year he was posted to govern Tongzhou.
units.literal: After more than a year he governed Tong prefecture.

units.zh: 始少帝與契丹絕好，繼勛亦預其謀，及契丹主至闕，繼勛自鎮來朝，契丹責之。
units.en: When the young emperor broke with the Khitans, Jixun had helped plan it. When the Khitan ruler reached the capital, Jixun came from his post to court, and the Khitans rebuked him.
units.literal: Earlier, when the Young Emperor broke with the Khitans, Jixun also took part in the plot. When the Khitan ruler reached the capital, Jixun came from his post to court and the Khitans reproached him.

units.zh: 時馮道在側，繼勛事急，指道曰：「少帝在鄴，道為首相，與景延廣謀議，遂致南北失歡。
units.en: Feng Dao stood nearby. In his panic Jixun pointed at him and said, "When the young emperor was at Ye, Dao was chief minister and plotted with Jing Yanguang, which is what ruined relations between north and south.
units.literal: Feng Dao was then at his side. Jixun, in his extremity, pointed at Dao and said: "When the Young Emperor was at Ye, Dao was chief minister and plotted with Jing Yanguang, thereby causing north and south to lose harmony.

units.zh: 臣位至卑，未嘗措言，今請問道，道細知之。」
units.en: My rank was too low for me to speak then. Question Dao—he knows every detail."
units.literal: My post was utterly low and I never spoke a word. Now I ask that Dao be questioned—Dao knows the details."

units.zh: 契丹主曰：「此老子不是好鬧人，無相牽引，皆爾輩為之。」
units.en: The Khitan ruler said, "This old man is no troublemaker—do not implicate him. You people did it yourselves."
units.literal: The Khitan ruler said: "This old fellow is not one to make trouble—do not drag him in. You lot did it all."

units.zh: 繼勛不敢復對。
units.en: Jixun did not dare answer further.
units.literal: Jixun dared not reply again.

units.zh: 繼勛時有疾，契丹主因令人候其疾狀，雲有風痹，契丹主曰：「北方地涼，居之此疾可愈。」
units.en: Jixun was ill at the time, and the Khitan ruler sent someone to inquire; he was told Jixun had rheumatic paralysis. The Khitan ruler said, "The north is cool—live there and the illness will pass."
units.literal: Jixun was then ill, and the Khitan ruler had someone inquire after his condition; it was reported that he had wind paralysis. The Khitan ruler said: "The northern lands are cool; living there this illness can be cured."

units.zh: 乃命鎖繼勛。
units.en: He then ordered Jixun shackled.
units.literal: He then ordered Jixun put in chains.

units.zh: 尋解之，以疾終於家。
units.en: He was soon released and died of illness at home.
units.literal: Soon he was released and died of illness at home.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：契丹主聞趙在禮死，乃釋繼勛，繼勛憂憤而卒。）〉
units.en: (Comprehensive Mirror: When the Khitan ruler heard of Zhao Zaili's death, he released Jixun, who then died of grief and resentment.)〉
units.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: When the Khitan ruler heard that Zhao Zaili had died, he then released Jixun; Jixun died of grief and anger.)〉

units.zh: 漢高祖入汴，贈太尉。
units.en: When Han Gaozu entered Bian, Jixun was posthumously made grand commandant.
units.literal: When Han Gaozu entered Bian, he was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 鄭受益，
units.en: Zheng Shouyi,
units.literal: Zheng Shouyi,

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書·宰相世系表》：字謙光。）〉
units.en: (New Book of Tang, Tables of Chief Ministers' Lineages: styled Qianguang.)〉
units.literal: (New Book of Tang, Tables of Chief Ministers' Lineages: style Qianguang.)〉

units.zh: 唐宰相餘慶之曾孫也。
units.en: He was a great-grandson of Yuqing, a Tang chief minister.
units.literal: He was a great-grandson of Yuqing, chief minister of Tang.

units.zh: 余慶生浣，浣生從讜，兩為太原節度使，再登相位。
units.en: Yuqing's son was Huan; Huan's son was Congdan, who twice served as military governor of Taiyuan and twice rose to chief minister.
units.literal: Yuqing begot Huan; Huan begot Congdan, who twice was military governor of Taiyuan and twice reached the chief ministership.

units.zh: 從讜兄處誨，為汴州節度使。
units.en: Congdan's elder brother Chuhui was military governor of Bianzhou.
units.literal: Congdan's elder brother Chuhui was military governor of Bian prefecture.

units.zh: 家襲清儉，深有士風，中朝禮法，以鄭氏為甲。
units.en: The family was known for austerity and integrity and for true scholarly bearing; at court the Zheng were regarded as foremost in ritual propriety.
units.literal: The family inherited purity and frugality and had a deep gentleman's air; in court ritual and law the Zheng clan ranked first.

units.zh: 處誨生受益。
units.en: Chuhui was Shouyi's father.
units.literal: Chuhui begot Shouyi.

units.zh: 受益亦以文學致身，累歷臺閣，自尚書郎遷右諫議大夫。
units.en: Shouyi likewise rose through scholarship, served in a series of central offices, and was promoted from director in the masters of writing to right remonstrance adviser.
units.literal: Shouyi also rose through literary learning, passing through the terrace offices in succession, and from director in the Masters of Writing was promoted to right remonstrance adviser.

units.zh: 天福七年夏，以張彥澤數為不道，上章請行國典，旬日不報。
units.en: In the summer of the seventh Tianfu year, citing Zhang Yanzhe's repeated outrages, he memorialized that the law be enforced against him; for ten days the court gave no answer.
units.literal: In the summer of the seventh year of Tianfu, because Zhang Yanzhe had repeatedly acted against the Way, he memorialized asking that the national statutes be applied; for ten days there was no reply.

units.zh: 又貢表切言，訐直無所忌，執政稍惡之。
units.en: He submitted another memorial speaking bluntly and without fear, and the chief ministers grew to dislike him.
units.literal: He again presented a memorial speaking bluntly, exposing wrongs without reserve, and those in power gradually came to dislike him.

units.zh: 俄而以病請告，歸長安。
units.en: Soon he asked leave for illness and returned to Chang'an.
units.literal: Soon he asked leave on grounds of illness and returned to Chang'an.

units.zh: 高祖晏駕，以不赴國哀停任，會赦，拜京兆少尹。
units.en: When Gaozu died he was suspended for failing to attend the state mourning; after an amnesty he was appointed vice prefect of the capital district.
units.literal: When Gaozu died he was suspended from office for not attending the national mourning; when an amnesty came he was appointed vice prefect of the capital district.

units.zh: 宰相趙瑩出鎮鹹秦，以受益朝班舊僚，眷待甚至。
units.en: When chief minister Zhao Ying was posted to Xian and Qin, he treated Shouyi, an old court colleague, with exceptional favor.
units.literal: Chief minister Zhao Ying went out to govern Xian and Qin and, because Shouyi was an old colleague from court, treated him with exceptional favor.

units.zh: 屬天下率借金谷，乃謂瑩曰：「京兆戶籍登耗，民力虛實，某備知之矣，品而定之，可使平允。」
units.en: When the empire levied grain and cash loans, he told Ying, "I know the capital district's household registers, gains and losses, and the people's real capacity. Grade them properly and the levies can be made fair."
units.literal: When the empire levied loans of grain and cash, he said to Ying: "The capital district's household registers, gains and losses, and the people's strength, empty or full—I know them all. Grade and fix them and fairness can be achieved."

units.zh: 瑩信之，因使與王人同掌其事。
units.en: Ying believed him and therefore had him manage the matter jointly with the imperial commissioner.
units.literal: Ying trusted him and therefore had him jointly manage the matter with the king's commissioner.

units.zh: 受益既經廢棄，薄於仕宦，遂阿法射利，冀為生生之資；
units.en: Having already been cast aside, Shouyi cared little for office and bent the law for profit, hoping to secure a living;
units.literal: Shouyi, having already been cast aside, was indifferent to office and therefore bent the law to seek profit, hoping for means of livelihood;

units.zh: 又素恃門望，陵轢同幕，內奸外直，群情無相洽者。
units.en: he also relied on his family's prestige, bullied colleagues on the staff, was treacherous within and upright in appearance, and won the goodwill of none around him.
units.literal: he also by nature relied on his family's standing, bullied his colleagues on the staff, was inwardly treacherous and outwardly upright, and among the group none were on good terms with him.

units.zh: 及贓汙事發，騰於眾口，瑩不得已，遂按之，其直百萬。
units.en: When the bribery scandal broke and public outcry mounted, Ying had no choice but to investigate; the sum involved reached a million cash.
units.literal: When the bribery affair broke out it spread on every tongue; Ying had no choice but to investigate, and the value reached a million.

units.zh: 八年冬，賜死於家。
units.en: In the winter of the eighth year he was ordered to take his own life at home.
units.literal: In the winter of the eighth year he was granted death at home.

units.zh: 受益數世公臺，一朝自棄，士君子皆惜之。
units.en: For generations his family had held the highest offices, yet in a single stroke he ruined himself, and men of worth all lamented it.
units.literal: Shouyi's family for generations had held the highest offices, yet in a single morning he threw himself away; gentlemen all regretted it.

units.zh: 程遜，字浮休，壽春人。
units.en: Cheng Xun, styled Fuxiu, was from Shouchun.
units.literal: Cheng Xun, style Fuxiu, was a man of Shouchun.

units.zh: 〈（案：此下有闕文。）〉
units.en: (Editor's note: the passage below is missing.)〉
units.literal: (Note: text is missing below.)〉

units.zh: 召入翰林充學士，自兵部侍郎承旨授太常卿。
units.en: He was summoned to the Hanlin as an academician and promoted from vice minister of war with drafting duties to minister of imperial sacrifices.
units.literal: He was summoned into the Hanlin as academician, and from vice minister of War with drafting duties was appointed minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 天福三年秋，命使吳越，
units.en: In the autumn of the third Tianfu year he was ordered as envoy to Wu and Yue,
units.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Tianfu he was ordered as envoy to Wu and Yue,

units.zh: 〈（《十國春秋》云：禮部尚書程遜為加恩使。）〉
units.en: (Ten States Spring and Autumn records that Minister of Rites Cheng Xun served as grace-bestowing envoy.)〉
units.literal: (Ten States Spring and Autumn says: Minister of Rites Cheng Xun served as grace-bestowing envoy.)〉

units.zh: 母羸老雙瞽，遜未嘗白執政以辭之。
units.en: His mother was frail, elderly, and blind in both eyes, yet Xun never asked the chief ministers to excuse him from the mission.
units.literal: His mother was frail and old and blind in both eyes; Xun never told those in power to decline the mission on that account.

units.zh: 將行，母以手捫其面，號泣以送之。
units.en: When he was about to leave, his mother stroked his face with her hands and wept as she sent him off.
units.literal: As he was about to depart, his mother felt his face with her hands and wailed as she sent him off.

units.zh: 仲秋之夕，陰暝如晦，遜嘗為詩曰：「幽室有時聞雁叫，空庭無路見蟾光。」
units.en: One mid-autumn evening the sky was dark as dusk. Xun once wrote a poem: "In a secluded room wild geese sometimes cry; in an empty courtyard no path leads to the moonlight."
units.literal: On a mid-autumn evening the gloom was dark as twilight. Xun once wrote a poem: "In a secluded room one sometimes hears the wild geese call; in an empty courtyard there is no path to see the moon's light."

units.zh: 同僚見之，訝其詩語稍異。
units.en: Colleagues who read it were struck by how odd the lines sounded.
units.literal: His colleagues who saw it were surprised that the poem's language was somewhat strange.

units.zh: 及使回，遭風水而溺焉。
units.en: On the return journey he was lost in wind and waves and drowned.
units.literal: When the mission returned he met wind and waves and drowned.

units.zh: 李郁，字文緯，唐之宗屬也。
units.en: Li Yu, styled Wenwei, was a member of the Tang imperial clan.
units.literal: Li Yu, style Wenwei, was a kinsman of Tang.

units.zh: 少歷宗寺官，天成、長興中，累遷為宗正卿。
units.en: In youth he served in the clan temple offices; during Tiancheng and Changxing he rose step by step to director of the imperial clan court.
units.literal: In youth he passed through offices of the clan temple; during Tiancheng and Changxing he was promoted in succession to director of the Imperial Clan Court.

units.zh: 性平允，所歷無愛憎毀譽。
units.en: He was even-tempered and fair-minded; in every post he aroused neither special favor nor hostility, neither praise nor blame.
units.literal: His nature was even and fair; in every post he drew neither favor nor hatred, neither praise nor blame.

units.zh: 高祖登極，授光祿卿。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne he was appointed minister of imperial entertainments.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was made Minister of Imperial Entertainments.

units.zh: 一日晝寢，夢食巨棗，覺而有疾，謂其親友曰：「嘗聞『棗』字重『來』，呼魂之象也。
units.en: One afternoon he napped and dreamed of eating huge jujubes. When he woke he fell ill and told his friends, "They say the character for 'jujube' contains the character for 'come'—a sign that one's soul is being summoned back.
units.literal: One day he napped by day and dreamed of eating huge jujubes. On waking he fell ill and told his kin and friends: "I have heard that the character zao ('jujube') contains the character lai ('come')—a sign of calling back the soul.

units.zh: 余神氣逼抑，將不免乎！」
units.en: My spirit feels crushed—I shall not escape death!"
units.literal: My vital spirit is pressed down—I shall not escape death!"

units.zh: 天福五年夏卒。
units.en: He died in the summer of the fifth Tianfu year.
units.literal: He died in the summer of the fifth year of Tianfu.

units.zh: 贈太子太保。
units.en: He was posthumously made grand tutor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 馬重績，字洞微。
units.en: Ma Zhongji, styled Dongwei.
units.literal: Ma Zhongji, style Dongwei.

units.zh: 少學數術，明太一、五紀、八象、三統大歷，居於太原。
units.en: From youth he studied numerology and mastered the Great One, Five Registers, Eight Images, and Great Calendar of the Three Unifications; he lived at Taiyuan.
units.literal: In youth he studied numerology and was versed in the Great One, the Five Registers, the Eight Images, and the Great Calendar of the Three Unifications; he lived at Taiyuan.

units.zh: 仕晉，拜太子右贊善大夫，遷司天監。
units.en: Under Jin he was appointed right mentor of the heir apparent and then director of the astronomy bureau.
units.literal: Serving Jin, he was made Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent and transferred to director of the Astronomy Bureau.

units.zh: 天福三年，重績上言：「歷象，王者所以正一氣之元，宣萬邦之命，而古今所記，考審多差。
units.en: In the third Tianfu year Zhongji memorialized, "Calendars and celestial observations are how kings set the origin of cosmic order and proclaim the mandate to all states, yet records ancient and modern, when examined closely, contain many errors.
units.literal: In the third year of Tianfu, Zhongji memorialized: "The calendar and celestial signs are what kings use to rectify the origin of the single qi and proclaim the mandate to the myriad states, yet what ancient and modern records preserve, on examination, contains many errors.

units.zh: 《宣明》氣朔正而星度不驗，《崇元》五星得而歲差一日。
units.en: The Xuanming calendar's qi phases and new moons are correct, but its star positions fail verification; the Chongyuan tracks the five planets correctly but the year is off by a day.
units.literal: The Xuanming calendar's qi and new moons are correct but the star degrees do not check; the Chongyuan gets the five planets right but the year differs by a day.

units.zh: 以《宣明》之氣朔，合《崇元》之五星，二歷相參，然後符合。
units.en: Combine the Xuanming calendar's qi phases and new moons with the Chongyuan's planetary tables; only when the two calendars are cross-checked do they agree.
units.literal: Take the qi and new moons of the Xuanming and combine them with the five planets of the Chongyuan; when the two calendars are cross-checked, then they accord.

units.zh: 自前世諸歷，皆起天正十一月為歲首，用太古甲子為上元，積歲愈多，差闊愈甚。
units.en: Earlier calendars all began the year in the eleventh month of the celestial standard and used the primordial jiazi cycle as the superior origin; the more years accumulated, the wider the error grew.
units.literal: From former ages all calendars have taken the eleventh month of the celestial standard as year-start and used the primordial jiazi cycle as superior origin; the more years accumulate, the wider the discrepancy grows.

units.zh: 臣輒合二歷，創為新法，以唐天寶十四載乙未為上元，雨水正月中氣為氣首。」
units.en: I have combined the two calendars into a new method, taking the yiwei year (Tang Tianbao 14) as the superior origin and the mid-qi of the first month of Rain Water as the start of the qi cycle."
units.literal: Your servant has combined the two calendars and created a new method, taking the yiwei year, the fourteenth year of Tang Tianbao, as superior origin and the mid-qi of the first month of Rain Water as the head of qi."

units.zh: 詔下司天監趙仁琦、張文皓等考核得失，仁琦等言：「明年庚子正月朔，用重績歷考之，皆合無舛。」
units.en: The court ordered Zhao Renqi, Zhang Wenhao, and others at the astronomy bureau to review it. They reported, "On the new year's day of the coming gengzi year, Zhongji's calendar matches observation in every respect."
units.literal: An edict sent the matter to Zhao Renqi, Zhang Wenhao, and others of the Astronomy Bureau to examine gains and losses. Renqi and the rest said: "On the new moon of the first month of next year, the gengzi year, if examined by Zhongji's calendar, all will accord without error."

units.zh: 乃下詔班行之，號《調元曆》。
units.en: An edict was issued to promulgate it under the title Calendar for Adjusting the Origin.
units.literal: An edict was then issued to promulgate it; it was titled the Calendar for Adjusting the Origin.

units.zh: 行之數歲輒差，遂不用。
units.en: After a few years in use it began to drift, and the court abandoned it.
units.literal: After a few years in use it soon showed discrepancy and was then abandoned.

units.zh: 重績又言：「漏刻之法，以中星考晝夜為一百刻，八刻六十分刻之二十為一時，時以四刻十分為正，此自古所用也。
units.en: Zhongji also argued, "The clepsydra method divides day and night into one hundred marks by observing culmination stars; eight marks plus twenty sixtieths make one double-hour, with the fourth mark and ten parts as the standard—this is the ancient practice.
units.literal: Zhongji also said: "The method of clepsydra graduations takes the culmination stars to divide day and night into one hundred ke; eight ke and twenty sixtieths of a ke make one double-hour, and the double-hour takes the fourth ke and ten parts as correct—this is what has been used since antiquity.

units.zh: 今失其傳，以午正為時始，下侵未四刻十分而為午，由是晝夜昏曉，皆失其正，請依古改正。」
units.en: That tradition is now lost: noon is taken as the start of the hour, pushing true noon down into the fourth mark and ten parts of the wei period, so day, night, dusk, and dawn are all wrong. I ask that the ancient method be restored."
units.literal: Now the transmission is lost: they take noon as the start of the double-hour and push noon down into the fourth ke and ten parts of wei, so that day, night, dusk, and dawn all lose their correctness. I ask that it be corrected according to antiquity."

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: The court agreed.
units.literal: The request was granted.

units.zh: 重績卒年六十四。
units.en: Zhongji died at sixty-four.
units.literal: Zhongji died at the age of sixty-four.

units.zh: 陳元，京兆人也。
units.en: Chen Yuan was a native of the capital district.
units.literal: Chen Yuan was a man of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 家世為醫，初事河中王重榮。
units.en: His family had practiced medicine for generations; he first served Wang Chongrong of Hezhong.
units.literal: His family for generations practiced medicine; at first he served Wang Chongrong of Hezhong.

units.zh: 乾符中，後唐武皇自太原率師攻王行瑜，路出於蒲中，時元侍湯藥，武皇甚重之。
units.en: During Qianfu, Later Tang's martial emperor marched from Taiyuan against Wang Xingyu and passed through Pu. Yuan attended him with medicines, and the martial emperor held him in high regard.
units.literal: During Qianfu, Later Tang's Martial Emperor led troops from Taiyuan to attack Wang Xingyu, passing through Pu. Yuan then attended him with medicines and decoctions, and the Martial Emperor greatly valued him.

units.zh: 及還太原，日侍左右。
units.en: When the emperor returned to Taiyuan, Yuan attended him daily.
units.literal: When he returned to Taiyuan he attended him daily at his side.

units.zh: 武皇性剛暴，樂殺人，無敢言者。
units.en: The martial emperor was fierce and violent by nature and delighted in killing; no one dared remonstrate with him.
units.literal: The Martial Emperor by nature was fierce and violent, delighted in killing, and none dared speak to him.

units.zh: 元深測其情，每有暴怒，則從容啟諫，免禍者不一，以是晉人深德之，勛貴賂遺盈門。
units.en: Yuan read his moods well; whenever rage seized him, Yuan would calmly remonstrate and save many from death. The people of Jin were deeply grateful, and gifts from nobles filled his gate.
units.literal: Yuan deeply gauged his moods; whenever there was violent rage he would calmly remonstrate, and not a few were spared calamity. For this the people of Jin deeply thanked him, and meritorious nobles' gifts filled his gate.

units.zh: 性好酒樂施，隨得而無私積。
units.en: He loved wine and delighted in giving away whatever came to hand, keeping nothing for himself.
units.literal: By nature he loved wine and delighted in giving; whatever he received he kept no private store.

units.zh: 明宗朝，為太原少尹，入為太府卿。
units.en: Under Mingzong he served as vice prefect of Taiyuan, then entered the capital as minister of the imperial storehouse.
units.literal: In the reign of Mingzong he was vice prefect of Taiyuan and entered the capital as minister of the Imperial Storehouse.

units.zh: 長興中，集平生所驗方七十五首，並修合藥法百件，號曰《要術》，刊石置於太原府衙門之左，以示於眾，病者賴焉。
units.en: During Changxing he compiled seventy-five prescriptions he had tested in life and a hundred compounding methods under the title Essential Methods, had them carved on stone and set to the left of the Taiyuan government gate for all to see; the sick benefited from them.
units.literal: During Changxing he collected seventy-five prescriptions he had verified in his lifetime, together with a hundred methods of compounding medicines, titled Essential Methods, carved them on stone and set them to the left of the Taiyuan prefectural yamen gate to show the public; the sick relied on them.

units.zh: 天福中，以耄期上表求退，以光祿卿致仕，卒於晉陽，年八十餘。
units.en: In his old age during Tianfu he memorialized to retire and left office as minister of imperial entertainments; he died at Jinyang in his eighties.
units.literal: During Tianfu, in his great age, he memorialized asking to retire and left office as Minister of Imperial Entertainments; he died at Jinyang aged more than eighty.

units.zh: 史臣曰：夫彰善癉惡，《麟史》之為義也；
units.en: The historian writes: To make virtue plain and vice hateful is the purpose of the Spring and Autumn Annals;
units.literal: The historiographer says: To make good manifest and evil hateful is the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals;

units.zh: 瑜不掩瑕，虹玉之為德也。
units.en: not to hide a flaw in jade is the virtue of a true gem.
units.literal: not to cover a flaw in jade is the virtue of the rainbow gem.

units.zh: 故自崇弼而下，善者既書之，其不善者亦書之，庶使後之君子見善如不及，見惡如探湯也。
units.en: Therefore from Chongbi onward, virtues are recorded and faults are recorded as well, so that later gentlemen may strive toward good as if they cannot catch it and shrink from evil as from scalding water.
units.literal: Therefore from Chongbi downward, what was good has been written, and what was not good has also been written, so that later gentlemen may see good as if unable to reach it and see evil as if plunging the hand into boiling water.

units.zh: 至如重績之曆法，陳元之醫道，亦不可漏其名而弗紀也。
units.en: As for Zhongji's calendrical science and Chen Yuan's medical art, their names too must not be omitted from the record.
units.literal: As for Zhongji's calendrical method and Chen Yuan's medical art, their names likewise cannot be omitted and left unrecorded.

candidatePacket.instructions: Review dates, event ownership, conversions, endpoint evidence, age reckoning, omitted life dates, and active-date hints. Read all Chinese units for omissions; English is not independent evidence. Do not re-extract names or mentions. For each item identify whose event is dated and justify each endpoint. Same mother does not imply same birth year. Later allusions are not personal activity. Research or record a blocker rather than invent precision. A report cannot approve with missing checks or unresolved research.

findings.problem: Tianfu-era source wording is repeatedly extended through AD 944, although Later Jin Tianfu ended in AD 942; the derived active-date hints repeat that unsupported endpoint.
findings.action: Correct each Tianfu conversion to the supported AD 936–942 era or a narrower source-supported phase, then recompute the affected active-date hints without extending them into Kaiyun.

findings.problem: Kinship, retrospective ruler labels, and bare dynasty-office references have been converted into personal Western intervals without a dated event for the named person.
findings.action: Preserve the relationship or office wording as an undated source attestation, remove the invented Western intervals and active hints, and use a research hold only where independent evidence is required.

findings.problem: The named accession of the Later Tang Last Emperor is an AD 934 event, but several claims flatten it into the whole AD 934–936 reign and propagate that interval into hints.
findings.action: Use the single AD 934 accession context for these dated appointment events and recompute the affected hints; retain a wider interval only where the Chinese actually says a reign-long or phase-long period.

findings.problem: Phase and multi-year expressions are represented with mismatched precision: Tiancheng late is flattened to the full era, Liu Suiqing’s exact second year is labelled “before and after,” and Tianfu years seven through eight are reduced to AD 942.
findings.action: Preserve each Chinese phase or multi-year span conservatively: use an appropriate phase interval for Tiancheng late, correct the exact Tianfu-second-year source label, and encode the seventh-through-eighth-year context across AD 942–943 before recomputing hints.

findings.problem: Zhuangzong’s entry into Bian is a specific AD 923 event, but the record assigns Liu Suiqing a full AD 923–926 reign interval and presents it as active chronology.
findings.action: Replace the borrowed reign-wide interval with the single AD 923 event context and recompute Liu Suiqing’s active-date hint from the corrected claim.
